reasons: no_second_line: question two has no answer: no other line was seriously considered, which is R213's readiness test and the slice fails it
intent_insensitive: question four is no: a different enemy intent would not have changed the line, so the intent is not part of the decision

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Dodoco Blast for its guaranteed 7 damage to all enemies, then played Kaboom! on Twig Slime (S) to finish it after Dodoco Blast reduced it to 2 HP, and finally played Duck and Cover for 5 Block. This used the 2 available Sparks and 2 of 3 Energy, leaving 1 Energy unused because no other playable card remained.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up the chance to play Bang Bang! instead of Dodoco Blast, since both spend the same 2 Sparks and only one could be played. It also left 1 Energy unused, but there was no remaining card that could spend it.
answers.q4_different_intent: No. The chosen line was driven mainly by resource use, guaranteed damage, killing the lowest-HP attacker, and gaining Block. A different telegraphed intent would not have made another affordable line clearly better, because Dodoco Blast plus Kaboom! plus Duck and Cover still provided the strongest guaranteed damage and the only Block available.

survives_means: not yet falsified -- this funnel refuses turns and never rates them

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
targets.repair: out of scope by M63: this refuses a form and never repairs one

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
